Site permutations that keep the structure of a torus

Source: R/landscape.R
torus_permutations.Rd

The translations of a torus combined with the symmetries of the grid keep all distances among sites, and therefore the spatial autocorrelation of the environment. They give a restricted null model for spatially explicit metacommunities (see the vignette), as the torus-translation test of Harms et al. (2001). A square grid has eight symmetries and a rectangular one four. Sites are numbered with the first coordinate running fastest, as in expand.grid(x, y) and landscape_grid(). A real landscape has edges, and this null treats opposite edges as adjacent: see rigid_permutations() and patch_permutations().

Usage

torus_permutations(side, symmetries = TRUE, n_perm = NULL)

Arguments

side

Number of cells per side, as in landscape_grid(), or two numbers for a rectangular grid, the first for the coordinate that runs fastest.

symmetries

Combine the translations with the reflections and rotations of the grid?

n_perm

Number of permutations to keep, drawn without replacement. The default keeps all of them.

Value

Integer matrix with one permutation of the site indices per row, excluding the identity (\(8\, \mathrm{side}^2 - 1\) rows on a square grid with side > 2).

References

Harms, K. E., Condit, R., Hubbell, S. P., & Foster, R. B. (2001). Habitat associations of trees and shrubs in a 50-ha neotropical forest plot. Journal of Ecology, 89, 947–959.

See also

Other restricted null models: patch_permutations(), rigid_permutations()

Examples

p <- torus_permutations(4)
dim(p)
#> [1] 127  16
dim(torus_permutations(c(6, 4), symmetries = FALSE))
#> [1] 23 24
